title: UK Balance of Payments, The Pink Book 2026 (ONS, 09:30 London) — the Blue Book's twin, published in the same slot
source: EST: ons.gov.uk/releases/ukbalanceofpaymentsthepinkbook2026, re-fetched direct 2026-10-16 (HTTP 200, 42,042 bytes) — reads verbatim 'Release date: 30 October 2026 9:30am' and 'This release is not yet published'; the 'Provisional' label the 2026-09-10 proposal read has been DROPPED by the ONS. Cadence scraped first-party the same session from the ONS Pink Book previous-releases page (HTTP 200): all ten editions 2016-2025 published on the LAST WORKING DAY of their month (2016-07-29, 2017-10-31, 2018-07-31, 2019-10-31, 2020-10-30, 2021-10-29, 2022-10-31, 2023-10-31, 2024-10-31, 2025-10-31), 10 of 10, and 2026-10-31 is a Saturday. Stays estimate: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no slot for a foreign national statistics institute, and this lane does not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN BY THE never-assessed INITIAL RESEARCH OF THIS EVENT, 2026-10-16, after reading the single prior proposal (from-uk-blue-book-2026-10-30) in full; the proposal's date, time and twin-slot claims all reproduce. What the initial adds: (1) the content is already public — the ONS Balance of payments, UK: April to June 2026 bulletin, released 2026-09-30, already applies the 'methods improvements for Blue Book and Pink Book 2026' (precious-metals reallocation, globalisation data from Q1 2024, 2024 ITIS survey), so the annual book binds numbers 30 days stale on the day; (2) a first-party event study of the ten Pink Book days against every other session since 2014 finds no series significantly above an ordinary day (IGLT.L 1.31x, t = 0.97; GBPUSD=X 0.89x; ^FTSE 0.61x; ^TNX 0.78x; SPY 0.84x; ^VIX 0.97x), the gilt ratio carried by Budget-adjacent editions; (3) the practical value to the corridor is still the proposal's own: a second ONS document landing two days after the 2026-10-28 Autumn Budget and FOMC, and so a second thing that could be misread as the cause of a 2026-10-30 gilt or sterling move that belongs to the Budget, the FOMC, the BoJ or ECI. LOW tier is inherited from the ONS family and the measured null. Estimate widens caution only; nothing date-keyed may act on this.
